body:
## Can we stay open during our Newcastle office refurbishment?

Some office refurbishments can be staged around business operations. Others need a temporary move, a closure period or a combination of arrangements. Decide from the actual works and the appointed team's assessment, rather than assuming that working after hours will resolve every impact.

Your Office Space provides client-side project management. We help organise the agreed brief, information, appointments, decisions and programme on the business's behalf. YOS does not carry out fitout construction as principal contractor, determine planning approval or certify that a building is safe to occupy. The appointed contractors and appropriately qualified advisers retain their respective roles.

[BUTTON: Plan my Newcastle refurbishment]

**Free working pack:** [Download the two-page checklist (PDF)](/guides/office-refurbishment-newcastle-stay-open-checklist.pdf) or [use the editable text version](/guides/office-refurbishment-newcastle-stay-open-checklist.txt). No email is required. The pack records questions, evidence and decisions for discussion with your appointed team; it is not an approval or safety certificate.

## Start with what must keep operating

List the functions your business cannot readily interrupt: customer contact, critical systems, confidential work, deliveries, accessible facilities and any specialist operations. Record when they are needed and what a temporary alternative would require.

Then ask the appointed construction and relevant specialist team whether those functions can be maintained alongside the proposed work. Keeping the business trading is an objective to test, not a safety conclusion that the business owner or this article can make alone.

## Compare three operating arrangements

| Arrangement | Business questions to resolve | Dependencies to confirm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stage works within the premises | Can usable space accommodate the team while another area is unavailable? | Separation, access, services, sequence and the responsible team's assessment |
| Temporarily relocate affected functions | Which teams, equipment and customer activities need an alternative location? | Suitable temporary space, IT, access, communication and return dates |
| Pause operations for defined work periods | Which activities can stop, and what must be arranged beforehand? | Customer notice, system arrangements, work scope and readiness before resuming |

The appropriate choice may combine these approaches. Compare total business disruption and coordination demands as well as the builder's programme. A short construction duration is not the full picture if staff need to move several times or services remain unavailable between stages.

## Plan the interfaces before selecting the staging option

Ask the appointed team to map the relationship between occupied areas, construction areas, deliveries, shared facilities and building access. Have the relevant advisers identify the implications for emergency arrangements, accessibility, services and people using the premises. Do not create your own site-separation or emergency plan from a generic checklist.

[SafeWork NSW's construction guidance](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/your-industry/construction/construction) covers construction responsibilities and risks, including essential services and traffic. The appropriate controls and responsibilities must be established by the parties responsible for the actual work and workplace. YOS's coordination role does not replace those duties.

In an older or uncertain building, obtain the relevant hazardous-material information before relying on the staging plan. [SafeWork NSW's asbestos guidance](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/hazards-a-z/asbestos) explains the need for appropriate professional assessment of suspected material. This guide does not provide instructions for inspecting, disturbing or removing it.

## Create an interruption register

For each proposed interruption, record the affected business function, provider responsible, proposed window, required approvals, customer or staff communication, backup arrangement and evidence needed before resuming the affected activity.

Include power, data, internet, phones, heating and cooling, access systems and other site-specific services where relevant. Ask the relevant providers about dependencies and restoration checks. A service being switched back on does not establish that all business systems are functioning as needed.

**Illustrative example, not a client case:** a meeting-room refurbishment affects the network equipment serving another part of the office. The interruption register should identify both the construction activity and the business systems affected, with the responsible providers confirming the agreed sequence and checks. Do not assume room boundaries match service boundaries.

[BUTTON: Discuss staging and business continuity]

## Ask the right questions about after-hours work

After-hours work may be useful for particular activities, but it does not automatically resolve site access, building restrictions, approvals, staff movement, noise effects or specialist trade availability. Ask the appointed team what can be completed, what remains between shifts and when the area is suitable for its intended use again.

Record any landlord or building-manager requirements and clarify which working assumptions are included in the quote. Compare staging, temporary protection, repeated mobilisation, moving, IT and temporary-workplace costs where applicable. They should not disappear simply because they sit outside the headline construction price.

Use our [Newcastle fitout cost guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) to organise budget questions and the [construction quote comparison guide](/blog/compare-office-construction-quotes-newcastle) to compare inclusions.

## Communicate decisions before they become disruptions

Nominate a business contact who can approve operational arrangements and communicate with staff. Agree who reports changes in the construction sequence and who confirms their implications with the business. Keep a decision record rather than relying on scattered messages.

Staff, visitors, customers and contractors may need different information. Establish an appropriate communication process with the appointed team, avoiding disclosure of private access or security details in general notices. Ask how changed access and facilities will be communicated to the people affected.

## Define the return-to-work evidence for each stage

Before a stage is treated as available, ask the responsible parties to identify the inspections, service checks, approvals and handover information needed for its intended use. Include any business systems and furniture that must be ready, and identify who accepts outstanding items.

Cleaning, furniture placement or a contractor leaving the site does not by itself settle whether the area can be occupied. Use the [fitout handover checklist](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist) alongside project-specific advice and documents.

## A refurbishment continuity checklist

- Identify critical business functions and their operating periods.
- Compare staging, temporary relocation and planned closures.
- Have the responsible team assess occupied-site feasibility.
- Obtain relevant building and hazardous-material information.
- Allocate access, shared-facility and service questions to the responsible advisers.
- Create an interruption register with an owner for each item.
- Record backup arrangements and restoration checks with the relevant providers.
- Confirm working windows, building requirements and quote assumptions.
- Agree staff, customer and contractor communication responsibilities.
- Track business moves and decisions alongside the construction programme.
- Define evidence required before each stage returns to use.
- Keep a contingency decision and escalation contact for changed circumstances.

## How client-side project management can help

Under an agreed engagement, YOS can help coordinate the operational brief, track decisions and connect the construction programme with staff moves, services, furniture and business approvals. We help keep the client informed about scope, budget and timing; we do not guarantee uninterrupted trading or take over the appointed providers' technical and safety responsibilities.

If you have not yet committed to the premises, start with the [fitout readiness guide](/blog/office-fitout-readiness-newcastle). For approval questions, read the [Newcastle fitout approvals guide](/blog/office-fitout-approvals-newcastle).

## Plan the operating arrangements before the start date

Tell us where the Newcastle office is, what needs changing, what must remain operational and the target timing. We can discuss the client-side coordination scope and information needed from the appointed project team.

## Common questions

### Can we keep working during a Newcastle office refurbishment?

It depends on the actual works, building, business functions and the responsible team’s assessment. Options may include staging, temporarily moving affected activities or planned closure periods. Do not assume a small project or after-hours work establishes that occupied working is suitable.

### Does after-hours construction remove the need to move staff?

Not necessarily. Dependencies may remain between shifts, including access, services, facilities and the condition of areas returning to use. Ask the appointed team to assess and document the proposed arrangement.

### What should an interruption register include?

Record the affected business function, responsible provider, proposed window, approval and communication needs, backup arrangements and the checks required before the activity resumes. Tailor the register to the actual workplace.

### Does YOS manage construction safety as the principal contractor?

No. YOS provides client-side coordination under an agreed engagement. The appointed contractor, business and relevant advisers retain their respective responsibilities; those responsibilities must be confirmed for the actual project.
